Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Nova Consumer Products Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing and asking questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Nova Consumer Products' Q3 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; David Kim, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Nova Consumer Products delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, sustainability initiatives, digital transformation, and outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $4.2 billion, representing a 5.2% increase compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 51.8%, driven by pricing actions, supply chain productivity, and favorable mix. Operating income was $850 million. Diluted earnings per share were $1.12. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me start with the top-line metric that underscores the health of our core business: organic sales growth. For those new to our calls, organic sales growth excludes the impacts of acquisitions, divestitures, foreign exchange, and one-time supply chain disruptions, giving a clean read on our underlying performance through volume, pricing, and mix shifts.

In Q3, we delivered organic sales growth of 5.2%, accelerating from 4.1% in Q2 and marking our third consecutive quarter of sequential improvement. This came in ahead of our internal expectations and street consensus of 4.6%, reflecting the resilience of our portfolio amid a still-challenging macro environment. Year-to-date, organic growth stands at 4.8%, positioning us well against the CPG industry average of around 3.5% as reported by NielsenIQ for the quarter.

Breaking this down further, let's dive into the decomposition of our organic sales growth: volume at +1.8%, price at +2.4%, and mix at +1.0%. This balanced profile reflects our disciplined execution across pricing discipline, premiumization strategies, and volume recovery through innovation and distribution gains.

Volume growth was the standout this quarter, up 180 basis points year-over-year, driven by market share expansion in 8 out of 10 core categories. We're gaining velocity in high-frequency categories like household cleaners and snacks, where we've outpaced category growth by 150 bps on average, per Nielsen and IRI data. Key initiatives include our product innovation pipeline, such as launches like NovaPure eco-friendly laundry pods—reformulated with 30% less water usage and bio-based enzymes—that drove +12% volume uplift in North American home care, capturing share from legacy brands like Tide Pods amid rising sustainability demands. Distribution expansion added 2.5 points of ACV globally, including e-commerce penetration now at 18% of sales, up from 14% last year. In Asia-Pacific, we secured listings with JD.com and Shopee for our nutrition bars, boosting impulse buys by 8%. Consumer activation through targeted in-store merchandising and shopper marketing, including AR-enabled shelf displays for our GlowBeauty skincare line, lifted household penetration by 4% in EMEA. Volumes were tempered by deliberate exits from low-margin SKUs—we divested 5% of our fabric care portfolio in Latin America—and softer discretionary spending in premium snacks, where U.S. volume dipped -1% due to trade-down to private labels.

Pricing delivered a solid contribution, moderating from Q2's +3.5% as input cost inflation eased to +4%, down from +7% peaks in 2022, per our supplier indices tracking commodities like palm oil and PET resin. We've clawed back 85% of cumulative inflation since 2021, aligning with industry leaders like Colgate-Palmolive. Everyday pricing actions included modest +1.8% list price increases on staples like dish soaps and bar soaps, with elasticities averaging -2.5, better than our -3.0 historical norm thanks to fortified value messaging, such as '2X cleaning power' claims validated by third-party lab tests. Full recovery in Nutrition, like protein shakes up +4.2% pricing where cocoa and whey costs rose 15% YoY. In contrast, Beauty held pricing flat to defend share against indie disruptors like The Ordinary. Promotional optimization reduced A&P funding on low-ROI promos by 20%, shifting to loyalty programs via our Nova Rewards app, which now has 25 million active users and improved promo ROI by 15%. Regionally, LatAm pricing popped +5.1% on aggressive actions in Brazil's high-inflation environment, while North America was more measured at +1.2% to avoid backlash.

Mix shift remains a core lever, contributing +100 bps for the third straight quarter, as consumers traded up to our 'Nova Elite' tier—now 22% of portfolio sales, up from 18% last year. This premiumization features higher-margin SKUs like our plant-based GlowBeauty serums at 45% gross margin versus 35% mass tier, and functional nutrition bars with adaptogens. Portfolio reshaping directed 60% of innovation dollars into premium, driving +3% mix in Beauty & Personal Care. Our anti-aging 'Retinol Renew' line gained 2 points of market share in Europe, per Kantar. Channel mix saw e-commerce and club channels like Costco and Sam's now 25% of sales, favoring premium packs with +15% price realization. APAC mix +2.1% from K-beauty inspired sheet masks in China offset -0.5% in U.S. snacks where value packs held firm.

By segment: Beauty & Personal Care, 42% of sales, +6.1% organic with volume +2.5%, price +2.6%, mix +1.0%, led by prestige skincare; U.S. share up 1.2 points. Home Care, 30%, +4.8% with volume +2.2%, price +1.9%, mix +0.7%, eco-launches shone in EMEA at +7.2%. Nutrition, 28%, +4.0% with volume +0.8%, price +2.8%, mix +0.4%, protein category softness hit volumes but pricing offset.

Regionally: North America +4.5% balanced, EMEA +6.8% volume-led, LatAm +7.2% pricing powerhouse, APAC +3.1% mix-driven despite China lockdowns.

This decomposition underscores our Resilient Growth Framework: protect core volumes through superiority via innovation and sustainability certifications like our 50% recyclable packaging goal, optimize pricing with data-led elasticity modeling leveraging AI tools like our PriceOptix platform, and accelerate mix via focused premium bets. We're on track for FY organic growth of 4.5-5.5%, with volume inflection expected in Q4 as U.S. consumer confidence stabilizes. Investments of $250 million in supply chain digitization and $150 million in direct-to-consumer platforms position us for margin expansion to 22%+ in FY24, even as deflation risks loom in commodities.

Turning to gross margin, which came in at 51.8% for the quarter—up 180 basis points year-over-year and 90 basis points sequentially from Q2. This marks our strongest quarterly expansion in over three years, exceeding our internal guidance midpoint of 50-51%. For the nine months year-to-date, gross margins stand at 51.2%, 210 basis points ahead of the prior year, positioning us toward our full-year target of 51-52%.

Pricing actions contributed approximately 320 basis points of expansion. In a high-inflation environment where U.S. CPI for food and beverages remains around 2.5%, we've executed disciplined, data-driven pricing across our portfolio. Beauty & Personal Care, including NovaGlow shampoos and EverFresh deodorants, saw list price increases of 4-6% in North America. Household Essentials prices on QuickClean wipes and EcoShield detergents rose 5% globally, with strong consumer acceptance shown by only modest volume softness of 1-2%.

Supply chain productivity and technical initiatives delivered another 150 basis points. Our NovaNext supply chain transformation integrates AI-driven demand forecasting with SAP S/4HANA ERP, reducing inventory obsolescence by 15% and improving production yields in aseptic packaging lines by 8%. New robotic palletizing systems at our Reno facility cut labor-intensive COGS by 12% for snacks. We're scaling regenerative agriculture partnerships—sourcing 40% of palm oil sustainably from Indonesia via RSPO-certified suppliers—stabilizing costs amid 25% YoY spike in palm oil futures.

Mix shift added 100 basis points, driven by premiumization. Power Brands like NovaPure organic baby foods and VitalEdge protein snacks grew 12% in revenue, outpacing company-wide organic growth. These higher-margin SKUs over 60% gross now represent 35% of North American portfolio, up from 28% last year.

Headwinds included commodity inflation shaving 120 basis points, led by cocoa surging 40% amid West African disruptions impacting Heritage ChocoBars, and dairy up 10% due to U.S. feed grain volatility. FX was a 30 basis point drag from stronger USD versus euro and Brazilian real. Freight rates remain 5% above pre-pandemic levels.

Regionally, North America delivered 53.2%, up 250 bps YoY, fueled by pricing and Amazon Fresh e-commerce mix at 18% of U.S. sales. EMEA at 49.5%, down 50 bps due to private-label competition from Aldi and Lidl plus energy surcharges, but Eastern Europe turnaround boosted margins 300 bps. APAC hit 52.1% from China premium skincare and India rural expansion.

This trajectory underscores our Margin First framework, targeting 54%+ by FY2026 through portfolio optimization—divesting low-margin legacy brands for $150 million to fund high-GMO innovations; digital supply chain with blockchain traceability for 70% of ingredients; and sustainability leverage like 50% recycled PET qualifying for EU Green Deal rebates.

Overall, Q3 was a standout amid dynamic CPG landscape. Total net sales reached $4.2 billion, up 7% year-over-year or 5% organic, our eighth consecutive quarter of positive organic growth outpacing industry 2-3%. Pricing contributed 4 points amid 8-10% input inflation on palm oil, cocoa, PET. Volume/mix +1%, with premiumization: EverClean plant-based laundry pods up 15% volume in North America, NutriBoost bars capturing health segment share. E-commerce 18% of revenue, up from 14%, via Amazon and Walmart+.

Adjusted gross margin expanded 210 bps to 53.2%, highest in five years, via $450 million supply chain savings, AI-optimized procurement, 20% logistics reduction through nearshoring in Mexico and Vietnam, offsetting 60% commodity inflation. Operating margin up 140 bps to 22.1%, adjusted operating income up 12% to $850 million. SG&A dipped to 31% via precision marketing improving digital ad ROI 25% targeting Gen Z.

Diluted EPS $1.12, up 14% YoY. Free cash flow $550 million, 13% of sales, enabling $300 million repurchases and 7% dividend hike—our 47th consecutive increase.

Segments: Beauty & Personal Care 38% sales, 8% organic, hair care +12%, fragrances +20%. Household & Fabric 32%, +6%, laundry +7% pricing. Food & Snacks 20%, 9% organic, savory +18%. Beverages 10%, 1% growth countered by zero-sugar +25%.

Regions: North America 45%, 4% organic, share +60 bps. EMEA 25%, 7%, sustainable packaging 80% recyclable. LatAm 15%, 11%. APAC 15%, 6%, China +4%, India +20%. FX shaved 2 points.

Strategic initiatives: Power of Three—consumer insights, superiority, productivity—150 bps share gain. Digital GenAI forecasting cut stockouts 30%, inventory to 65 days. Sustainability 25% Scope 3 reduction, NPS +8. Portfolio divest non-core for $1.2B, R&D 2.5% sales, 12 new platforms.

Before outlook, a note on competitive activity. The sector is intensely dynamic with inflation easing to 2.5% YoY, category growth low-single digits—snacks +3.2%, beverages +1.8% per NielsenIQ—but premium health +7-9%. Legacy like PepsiCo, Mondelez ramped promos to 22-25% revenue in NA. Private labels eroded branded share 120 bps in mass. Disruptors like Olipop, Perfect Snacks captured +15% e-comm health snacking. Unilever, Danone doubled sustainability. NA pricing wars with Pringles shaved our share 80 bps temporarily. APAC Nestlé KitKat localized innovation. EMEA HFSS regs, Reckitt gains.

Our responses: grew share +60 bps to 9.8%, +110 bps premium health. Precision pricing with SymphonyAI cut promo waste 18%, ACV 92%. Innovation six launches like FlexFuel energy drink +25% distribution. +3,200 facings at Kroger/Target, ESG packaging. E-comm ACoS down to 22%. Media ROI +25% CTV. Premiumization 42% portfolio >$3.50 RSP, margins +450 bps. Sustainability 95% recyclable by FY25. Data flywheel 15M loyalty users.

We're raising FY organic growth guidance to 4.5-6.0% from 4-5.5%, Q4 5.5-7%. Q3 guide was 3-5%, NA 4-6%, Europe 2-4%, EM 4-7%. H2 5%+ via launches, $250M reinvest. EPS $4.85-$4.95.

Following my remarks, Lisa will provide an update on our marketing and brand performance.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. We continue to see strong performance across our key brands. Our marketing investments are driving increased consumer engagement, and we are particularly pleased with the results of our recent Glow Up campaign. Precision pricing analytics and promo optimization, including AI-driven tools like PriceOptix, have preserved 85% MPS in core SKUs. Shopper marketing with AR displays and Nova Rewards app with 25 million users improved ROI 15%. Media spend flat at 11% revenue but ROI up 25% through CTV and retail media like Walmart Connect. Fuel Your Peak campaign garnered 500M impressions, +15% UPT among 25-34 demo. Sustainability creds boost loyalty, 72% Gen Z prioritize ESG per surveys. E-commerce partnerships expand bundles, Instacart same-day delivery.

After me, David will discuss our supply chain initiatives.

David Kim:
Thank you, Lisa. Our focus remains on optimizing our supply chain to enhance efficiency and resilience. We are implementing advanced analytics to improve forecasting and inventory management. NovaNext transformation integrates AI demand forecasting with SAP S/4HANA, reducing obsolescence 15%, yields +8%. Robotic palletizing cut COGS 12%. Localized 40% NA sourcing, lead times -25%. Regenerative ag 40% palm oil RSPO. Nearshoring Mexico/Vietnam -20% logistics. Blockchain traceability 70% ingredients. 50% recyclable packaging goal, 65% new launches carbon-neutral, 80% recyclable. Zero Waste Certified boosts loyalty 15% Europe.

Finally, Elena will share insights on our innovation pipeline.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, David. We are excited about the progress we are making on our new product development initiatives. Our pipeline is robust, and we are confident that our innovations will drive future growth. Our recent product, NovaPure EcoPods, is showing promising early results, with strong velocity and share gains.

Innovation is a cornerstone of our growth strategy. Successful NPD drives velocity, ACV, category-leading margins via premiumization and consumer-centric disruption. Q2 launches: PureThirst Zero zero-sugar electrolyte water, 85% NA distribution in 60 days, 42% repeat rate vs 30% benchmark, 25 units/store/week, $45M incremental YTD, 28% margin. Crunchy Bites PlantPower chickpea crisps, 62% EMEA ACV, 3.2 pts share UK/Germany, 18 units/store, €32M Q2, 4.2x ROI, 15g protein, regenerative sourcing. GlowEssence EcoBarrier reef-safe sunscreen, 72% APAC distribution, A$28M sales, 35% margin uplift, 40% wear-time extension.

Q2 NPD 22% segment revenue, up from 14%, 78% success vs 55% industry. Agile framework, 12-week tests, NielsenIQ AI insights.

Pipeline $250M R&D +18% YoY on functional nutrition, circular packaging, DTC personalization, climate-adaptive. H2 five launches: PureThirst Collagen Boost Q4 NA/LatAm, 35% trial intent, $120M FY25. Crunchy Bites KetoClusters Q1'25 US/Canada, 100% upcycled, 5% convenience share. GlowEssence AI-Skintone Serum DTC Q4, ML 50k microbiomes, €50M run-rate. NA 45% pipeline, EMEA +30% YoY EU Green Deal, APAC 22% organic affordability, LatAm localized flavors.

Rationalizing 15% low-velocity SKUs, biotech JV Dutch algae omega-3. 65% launches carbon-neutral.

NPD positions for 8-10% organic, 500bps mix improvement FY26.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions: press * then 1 to queue, *2 to withdraw. Our first question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs.

John Doe:
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce packaging waste and the associated cost savings?

David Kim:
Thanks for the question, John. Reducing packaging waste is central to our sustainability initiatives and operational efficiency. We've set a goal of 50% recyclable packaging, with 80% of products now recyclable, ahead of peers. Our Zero Waste Certified program and 65% carbon-neutral new launches have cut obsolescence 15% via better forecasting. Regenerative sourcing for 40% palm oil stabilized costs, and robotic systems reduced material waste. These efforts delivered $450 million in supply chain savings, including 20% logistics cuts, directly boosting gross margins by 150 bps. Cost savings from recycled PET and blockchain traceability for 70% ingredients hedge volatility, targeting further reductions as we scale circular packaging.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Smith with Morgan Stanley.

Jane Smith:
How are you leveraging data analytics to personalize your marketing efforts and improve customer engagement?

Lisa Patel:
Great question, Jane. Data analytics is transforming our marketing. Our Nova Rewards app with 25 million users provides zero-party data for hyper-personalized assortments, improving promo ROI 15%. SymphonyAI partnership enables dynamic pricing and CTV/retail media optimization, ROI +25%. Customer Decision Journey analytics target Gen Z on TikTok/Instagram, +15% UPT. AR shelf displays and Instacart partnerships boost penetration 4%. Velocity Scorecard benchmarks us leading 7/10 categories, with 500M impressions from campaigns like Fuel Your Peak. This drives 18% e-comm sales, loyalty metrics up, aligning with 72% Gen Z ESG priority.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Bob Johnson with JPMorgan.

Bob Johnson:
What is the expected impact of recent commodity price increases on your gross margins?

Michael Chen:
Thanks, Bob. Commodity inflation, like cocoa +40%, dairy +10%, palm oil +25%, shaved 120 bps this quarter, but we offset via 320 bps pricing, 150 bps productivity. Hedging covers 60% 2025 needs. Regenerative sourcing and alt-proteins mitigate. Q4 margins 52-53%, FY high-end 51-52%, targeting 54%+ FY26. If El Niño spikes ag costs, localized sourcing and blockchain hedge, but outlook assumes stable, supporting margin expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alice Lee with Barclays.

Alice Lee:
Can you discuss the competitive landscape and any emerging trends that are impacting your market share?

Sarah Thompson:
Alice, thanks for the question. The landscape is dynamic with inflation easing, low-single digit category growth, but premium health outpacing. Legacy promos up, private labels +120 bps erosion, disruptors e-comm strong, regional pressures like HFSS regs. We've grown share +60 bps overall, +110 bps premium via precision pricing -18% waste, innovation six launches +22% penetration, +3,200 facings, ACoS 22%, media ROI +25%. Premiumization 42% portfolio, sustainability 95% recyclable FY25, data flywheel. 4.2% organic vs industry 2.1%, margins held 42.3% despite $80M inflation. Confident +100 bps FY25 gains.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your thoughtful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to updating you next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Nova Consumer Products Q3 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Decomposition of organic sales growth: volume, price, mix
New product launches and innovation pipeline update
Organic sales growth guidance for next quarter/year

aspect_summary.Decomposition of organic sales growth: v: Organic sales growth of 5.2% decomposed into volume +1.8% (market share gains, innovation like NovaPure pods, distribution), price +2.4% (modest increases, inflation recovery), mix +1.0% (premiumization, Nova Elite tier). Balanced across segments: Beauty & Personal Care +2.5V/+2.6P/+1.0M; Home Care +2.2V/+1.9P/+0.7M; Nutrition +0.8V/+2.8P/+0.4M.
aspect_summary.New product launches and innovation pipe: Recent launches: NovaPure EcoPods (+12% volume in home care), PureThirst Zero (85% NA distribution, $45M YTD), Crunchy Bites PlantPower (62% EMEA ACV), GlowEssence EcoBarrier (72% APAC distribution). H2 pipeline: PureThirst Collagen Boost ($120M FY25), Crunchy Bites KetoClusters, GlowEssence AI-Skintone Serum; $250M R&D (+18% YoY), 22% segment revenue from NPD, 78% success rate.
aspect_summary.Competitive activity and response: Intense competition from PepsiCo/Mondelez promos (22-25% revenue), private labels (+120 bps share erosion), disruptors (Olipop +15% e-comm), Unilever/Danone sustainability, Pringles pricing wars, Nestlé localization. Response: +60 bps overall share/+110 bps premium, precision pricing (-18% promo waste), 6 launches (+22% penetration), +3,200 facings, e-comm ACoS 22%, media ROI +25%, premiumization (42% portfolio), 95% recyclable by FY25.
aspect_summary.Organic sales growth rate: Q3: 5.2% (accelerating from Q2 4.1%, ahead of 4.6% consensus); YTD: 4.8% (vs industry 3.5% per NielsenIQ); 8th consecutive positive quarter, outpacing industry 2-3%.
aspect_summary.Organic sales growth guidance for next q: FY raised to 4.5-6.0% (from 4-5.5%); Q4: 5.5-7%; H2: 5%+ via launches and $250M reinvestment.
aspect_summary.Gross margin percentage: Q3: 51.8% (up 180 bps YoY, 90 bps seq.); YTD: 51.2% (up 210 bps); FY target 51-52%; drivers: +320 bps pricing, +150 bps productivity, +100 bps mix; headwinds: -120 bps commodities.
aspect_summary.Overall company performance highlights: Net sales $4.2B (+5.2% reported, 5% organic); gross margin 51.8%; operating income $850M (+12% adj.); EPS $1.12 (+14%); FCF $550M (13% sales); share gains +60 bps; e-comm 18%; raised FY guidance; outpaced industry amid macro challenges.
